abstract:
Cilia are specialised cell-surface extensions central to signalling and sensation, and their dysfunction causes ciliopathies, a clinically heterogeneous group of disorders. Progress in the field has been held back by the lack of an updated and expanded gold-standard gene set.
We present CiliaHub, an open-access platform centered on an expert-curated catalog of over 2,500 ciliary and cilia-associated genes that significantly expands upon the scope of the SYSCILIA Gold Standard v2. For each gene, CiliaHub brings together subcellular localization, protein-complex information, domain architecture, cross-species orthology, functional-screen results, expression profiles, and ClinVar variants, as well as a dedicated ciliopathy module covering over 70 ciliopathies and over 400 disease genes. The data are queried through a rule-based question-answering assistant (CiliAI), gene-list analysis tools, a phenotype-driven search, and open static-JSON endpoints, supporting screen interpretation, variant prioritization, and ciliopathy research from a single point of access.
CiliaHub is freely available at https://ciliahub.org without registration. Source code is available on https://github.com/theCiliaHub/theCiliaHub.github.io and archived at Zenodo version 3 (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23257334). All figures and counts in this manuscript refer to CiliaHub release v9.2 (frozen October 2026). The versions of every external data source used in that release are listed in Supplementary Table S6, and the release version, freeze date and data file are stated at https://ciliahub.org/about.html.
Supplementary data are available at Zenodo online and static-JSON API endpoints (https://ciliahub.org/api.html).
